Combining AI CXR abnormality scores with symptom screening to select individuals for confirmatory molecular testing

links.outcome: TB cases detected and implementation costs compared with symptom screening
links.effect: Abnormality ≥ 0.50 detected 76 cases at US$56589, versus 77 cases at US$48939 for any symptom screening; the AI-only algorithm was strictly dominated.
links.quote: Abnormality ≥ 0.50 algorithm was strictly dominated as it led to 1 fewer diagnosis but costed more than the any symptom algorithm.

links.outcome: cost per case at varied prevalence
links.effect: AI screening had a lower cost per case detected than any-symptom screening only when the proportion of asymptomatic TB exceeded 30%.
links.quote: Our analysis showed that using CXR and AI had lower cost per case detected than any symptom screening criteria when asymptomatic TB was higher than 30% of all bacteriologically-confirmed TB detected.

links.effect: AI combined with symptom screening detected more cases at US$773 per case, whereas cough-only screening missed 60% of cases at US$1198 per case.
links.quote: The combined screening algorithm using both symptoms and CXR-AI detected more bacteriologically-confirmed cases at US$773 per case detected, whereas symptom-only screening criteria missed 60% cases at a much higher US$1198 per case detected cost for cough ≥ 2 weeks criteria and 10% missed cases at cost lower than CXR algorithm of US$636 per case detected.

screen.practice: alert threshold selection (AI abnormality score cutoffs combined with symptom screening)
screen.reason: Empirical implementation and cost-effectiveness study evaluating an AI chest X-ray tool (qXR) deployed in mobile lung health camps in Nigeria, comparing different AI triage thresholds (0.30 vs 0.50) and triage workflows against symptom screening.

primary.practice: threshold selection and triage algorithm design
